note: Figures are estimates. City sizes before 1950 follow Tertius Chandler's historical estimates; 1950–2010 follow UN World Urbanization Prospects (2018); 2025 follows the UN's 2025 update, which uses a new city definition. Economy rankings follow Angus Maddison's historical GDP estimates.

snaps.powers: Ming China is the world's richest state. The Ottomans are rising fast; Venice and Genoa run Mediterranean trade; Mali and Songhai control the Saharan gold trade.
snaps.money: Venetian gold ducat in the Mediterranean; Chinese silver and copper cash in East Asia
snaps.travel: No one sails the Atlantic. Venice to Alexandria takes about 3 weeks by galley.
snaps.news: As fast as a horse or a ship. News of Constantinople's fall (1453) took about a month to reach Venice.
snaps.dyk: Europeans and Americans have no idea the other continent exists.
snaps.relnote: No reliable global counts exist this early. The largest traditions were the mix of Confucian, Buddhist and folk practice in China, Hinduism in India, Islam from Morocco to Indonesia, and Christianity, then almost entirely in Europe and Ethiopia.

snaps.powers: Portugal has just opened the sea route to India. Spain is in the Caribbean. The Ottomans, Safavid Persia and the Ming dominate Eurasia; the Aztec and Inca empires are at their peak.
snaps.money: Venetian ducat and Portuguese gold; cowrie shells across much of Africa
snaps.travel: Columbus's first crossing (1492) took about 5 weeks.
snaps.news: Ship and horse. Word of Columbus's voyage took months to spread around Europe.
snaps.dyk: Tenochtitlan, with about 200,000 people, was bigger than any city in Spain.
snaps.relnote: Christianity is still mostly European; Islam is expanding in West Africa, India and Southeast Asia. Columbus's voyages are about to carry Christianity to the Americas.

snaps.powers: Habsburg Spain under Charles V and the Ottomans under Suleiman are the two superpowers of the Mediterranean world. The Mughals are taking hold in India.
snaps.money: Spanish silver from Potosí and Mexico starts flowing around the world
snaps.travel: Spain to the Caribbean: about 6–8 weeks by galleon.
snaps.news: Ship and horse; printed pamphlets now spread news within Europe in weeks.
snaps.dyk: Istanbul was Europe's largest city, by far.
snaps.relnote: The Reformation has split Western Christianity into Catholic and Protestant. Safavid Iran has made Shi'a Islam its state religion, deepening the Sunni–Shi'a divide.

snaps.state: Spain and Portugal, united under one king
snaps.powers: Spain is still the leading European power but is overstretched. The Dutch and English are rising at sea. Akbar's Mughal India is one of the richest states on Earth.
snaps.money: The Spanish silver 'piece of eight' becomes the first global currency
snaps.travel: About 6–8 weeks to cross the Atlantic.
snaps.news: Ship and horse; the first weekly newspapers appear in Germany in 1605.
snaps.dyk: Spanish silver was so central to China's economy that Ming taxes were paid in it.
snaps.relnote: Catholic missionaries are converting people across the Americas, the Philippines and parts of Japan and Africa. Akbar is hosting interfaith debates in India.

snaps.economy: Qing/Ming China, with Mughal India close behind
snaps.state: Tsardom of Russia (reached the Pacific in 1639)
snaps.powers: The Dutch Republic is the trading superpower. The Manchu Qing are conquering China; Europe is exhausted after the Thirty Years' War.
snaps.money: Spanish pieces of eight; Amsterdam is the world's banking center
snaps.news: Ship and horse; coffeehouses in London and Istanbul become news hubs.
snaps.dyk: World population actually fell between 1600 and 1650: war, plague and the Ming collapse.
snaps.relnote: Europe's wars of religion end with the Peace of Westphalia. Japan has banned Christianity.

snaps.economy: Mughal India (about a quarter of world output)
snaps.populous: Mughal India and Qing China, roughly tied
snaps.powers: Louis XIV's France dominates Europe. Mughal India is at its largest. Qing China is stable and growing under the Kangxi Emperor.
snaps.money: Spanish silver dollar; Indian cotton cloth is traded like currency in West Africa
snaps.news: Ship and horse; regular postal packet boats cross the Channel.
snaps.dyk: Edo, with about 700,000 people, was likely bigger than London or Paris.
snaps.relnote: Christianity is now the majority religion of the Americas. The Mughal emperor Aurangzeb has turned away from Akbar's tolerance.

snaps.powers: Britain and France fight for global supremacy. Qing China is at its height under Qianlong. The Mughal Empire is breaking apart.
snaps.money: Spanish silver dollar; the British pound starts to matter
snaps.news: Ship and horse; a letter from London to Boston takes 1–2 months.
snaps.dyk: The Atlantic slave trade was at its peak: tens of thousands of Africans were shipped every year.
snaps.relnote: Revival movements spread: the Great Awakening in Britain's colonies, Wahhabism in Arabia.

snaps.economy: Qing China (about a third of world output in 1820)
snaps.powers: Napoleon's France against Britain. Britain's Industrial Revolution is underway; Qing China is still the biggest economy.
snaps.money: Spanish silver dollar, the currency of the young USA too
snaps.news: Ship and horse; France's optical semaphore can relay a message 200 km in minutes.
snaps.dyk: About one in three people on Earth lived in Qing China.
snaps.relnote: Protestant missionary societies are founded and begin working in Africa and Asia. In West Africa, Islamic reform movements build new states like Sokoto.

snaps.economy: Qing China, but Britain leads in industry
snaps.powers: Britain is the 'workshop of the world' and rules the oceans. China is weakened by the Opium War and the Taiping Rebellion.
snaps.money: British pound sterling, backed by gold
snaps.news: The telegraph sends news across countries in minutes; the first lasting transatlantic cable comes in 1866.
snaps.dyk: London became the first modern city of over 2 million people.
snaps.relnote: Christian missions follow the expansion of empire into Africa and Asia; China's Taiping rebels mix Christianity with Chinese tradition.

snaps.powers: The British Empire is at its peak. The US and Germany have overtaken Britain in industry. Europe has carved up nearly all of Africa.
snaps.money: British pound, on the gold standard
snaps.news: Telegraph cables circle the globe; Marconi's radio crosses the Atlantic in 1901.
snaps.dyk: All five of the world's biggest cities were in Europe or the US for the first and only time.

snaps.powers: The US is the richest country but stays out of world politics. Britain and France hold huge empires. The USSR and fascist Italy are new.
snaps.money: Pound and dollar share the job
snaps.travel: About 5–6 days by liner. Lindbergh flies solo in 1927 (33 hours).
snaps.news: Radio brings news into homes; transatlantic phone calls start in 1927.
snaps.dyk: New York had just overtaken London as the world's largest city.

snaps.economy: United States (about a quarter of world output)
snaps.powers: Two superpowers: the US and the USSR. Europe's empires are starting to dissolve; India and China are newly independent or newly communist.
snaps.money: US dollar, pegged to gold (Bretton Woods)
snaps.news: Radio everywhere; TV spreading in the US.
snaps.dyk: Global life expectancy was about 46 years, up from about 30 in 1800.

snaps.powers: US vs USSR at the height of the Cold War. 17 African nations become independent in one year.
snaps.news: Television; the first communications satellite (Telstar) arrives in 1962.
snaps.dyk: World population hit 3 billion, only about 30 years after it hit 2 billion.

snaps.powers: Cold War détente. The US has just left Vietnam; OPEC's oil embargo shows the power of oil states.
snaps.money: US dollar, now floating (gold link cut in 1971)
snaps.travel: About 7 hours by jet; Concorde does it in 3.5 from 1976.
snaps.news: Satellite TV news; the first personal computers are being built in garages.
snaps.dyk: Mexico City and São Paulo had joined the world's five biggest cities.

snaps.state: Soviet Union, until it breaks up in 1991
snaps.powers: The Cold War ends; the US is the only superpower. Germany reunifies; apartheid is crumbling.
snaps.news: 24-hour cable news (CNN); Tim Berners-Lee invents the World Wide Web.
snaps.dyk: By the end of 1990 the World Wide Web had exactly one website, at CERN in Switzerland.

snaps.powers: US 'unipolar moment'. The EU prepares the euro; China is about to join the WTO.
snaps.money: US dollar; the euro launches (coins and notes in 2002)
snaps.news: The internet goes mainstream; about 6% of people are online.

snaps.economy: United States (China becomes number two this year)
snaps.powers: US still dominant but China rising fast. Europe in a debt crisis; the Arab Spring begins.
snaps.money: US dollar, with the euro second
snaps.news: Smartphones and social media; about 30% of people are online.
snaps.dyk: For the first time, more than half of humanity lived in cities (passed around 2007).

snaps.economy: United States (China largest by purchasing power)
snaps.powers: US–China rivalry dominates. Russia is at war in Ukraine; India is the most populous country.
snaps.news: Instant and global; about two-thirds of people are online.
snaps.dyk: Under the UN's new 2025 city definition, Jakarta is the world's largest city; Cairo is the only non-Asian city in the top ten.
